title: Which One? は/が, に/で, と/や, を/が
description: Contrast practice: the particle pairs N5 learners mix up most, side by side.

points.title: は vs が
points.summary: は = topic (known, 'as for …'). が = subject with focus (new info, question words, answers to が-questions, inside sub-clauses).
points.body:
Both can mark what looks like the subject, but they answer different questions.

**は (topic)** — sets up what the sentence is about; the important part comes *after* it:
- わたしは学生です。 (As for me — student.)
- Contrast: 肉は食べますが、魚は食べません。

**が (subject with focus)** — the important part is the *subject itself*:
- **Question words**: だれが来ましたか。 — never だれは.
- **Answering a が-question**: どれがあなたのですか。—これ**が**わたしのです。
- **Noticing / new information**: あ、財布が落ちていますよ。
- **Inside a sub-clause** (relative clause, とき, から…): 母**が**作った料理 — は is not used there.
- **Objects of 好き/わかる/ほしい/上手** (see を vs が).

Rule of thumb: if you could add 'it is X who/that…' in English, use が.
examples: だれが{窓|まど}を{開|あ}けましたか。—{田中|たなか}さんが{開|あ}けました。
Who opened the window? — Tanaka did.
{母|はは}が{作|つく}った{料理|りょうり}はおいしいです。
The food my mother made is delicious.
{肉|にく}は{食|た}べますが、{魚|さかな}は{食|た}べません。
Meat I eat, but fish I don't.

points.title: に vs で (place)
points.summary: に = where something IS (exists, lives) or the point something goes to/lands on. で = where something HAPPENS (actions, events).
points.body:
**に — location of existence / arrival point:**
- いる・ある・住む: 部屋**に**います, 東京**に**住んでいます.
- Where something ends up: 机の上**に**置く, 紙**に**書く, 駅**に**着く.

**で — location of an action or event:**
- 図書館**で**勉強する, 入口**で**靴を脱ぐ, 公園**で**遊ぶ.
- Events, even with ある: 体育館**で**コンサートがあります.

Quick test: is there a **verb of doing**? → で. Is it about **being / ending up somewhere**? → に.
examples: {本|ほん}は{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}にあります。
The book is on the desk.
{毎日|まいにち}{図書館|としょかん}で{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
I study at the library every day.
{入口|いりぐち}で{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}いでください。
Please take your shoes off at the entrance.

points.title: と vs や
points.summary: と = 'and' (complete list) or 'with' (a companion). や = 'and … among others' (incomplete list, nouns only).
points.body:
**と**:
- Complete list: 父**と**母**と**私の三人です — exactly these.
- 'With': 友達**と**映画を見ました.

**や**:
- Example list, others implied: 本**や**ノート**など**があります.
- Can't mean 'with' — 友達や映画を見ました would mean 'watched friends and movies'.

If the sentence counts or names *everyone/everything* (三人です, 全部), use と.
examples: {家族|かぞく}は{父|ちち}と{母|はは}と{私|わたし}の{三人|さんにん}です。
My family is three people: my father, my mother and me.
{友達|ともだち}と{一緒|いっしょ}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
I watched a movie with a friend.
かばんに{本|ほん}やノートなどが{入|はい}っています。
There are books, notebooks and so on in my bag.

points.title: を vs が (objects)
points.summary: Action verbs (食べる, 飲む, 買う) take を. Adjectives and state verbs (好き, 嫌い, 上手, ほしい, わかる, できる) take が.
points.body:
In English everything is just 'an object', but Japanese splits them:

**を** — object of an **action verb**: コーヒー**を**飲む, 本**を**読む, 日本語**を**勉強する.

**が** — the 'object' of **adjectives** and **state verbs**:
- 好き・嫌い: 猫**が**好き
- 上手・下手: 料理**が**上手
- ほしい: 車**が**ほしい
- わかる・できる: 日本語**が**わかる / できる
- ある (have): 時間**が**ある

These are among the most frequent learner errors: ✗ 日本語をわかります, ✗ 猫を好きです, ✗ 車をほしいです.
examples: {毎朝|まいあさ}コーヒーを{飲|の}みます。
I drink coffee every morning.
{日本語|にほんご}が{少|すこ}しわかります。
I understand a little Japanese.
{母|はは}は{料理|りょうり}が{上手|じょうず}です。
My mother is good at cooking.

questions.prompt: だれ（　）この{絵|え}を{描|か}きましたか。
notes: を would make 'who' the object of drawing.
だれも + positive verb isn't used.
Question words can't be topics — だれは is always wrong.

questions.prompt: A：どれがあなたのかばんですか。　B：これ（　）わたしのかばんです。
questions.explanation: Answering a **が**-question keeps **が** — the focus is on 'this one'.
notes: これは… states a fact about 'this', but doesn't answer *which one* — the question's focus is on the subject, so が.
を doesn't fit with です.
これも = 'this one too' — doesn't answer which one.
questions.translation: A: Which one is your bag? B: This one is my bag.

questions.prompt: {母|はは}（　）{作|つく}った{料理|りょうり}はとてもおいしいです。
questions.explanation: Inside a relative clause (母が作った → 料理), the subject takes **が**, not は.
notes: は can't mark the subject inside a noun-modifying clause.
で would mean 'by means of mother'.
を would make mother the thing cooked.
questions.translation: The food my mother made is very delicious.

questions.prompt: あ、{財布|さいふ}（　）{落|お}ちていますよ。
notes: 落ちる is intransitive — no を.
財布の落ちて isn't a sentence.
財布は… would treat the wallet as a known topic — but you've only just noticed it.
questions.translation: Oh, your wallet has fallen (on the floor).

questions.prompt: {毎日|まいにち}{図書館|としょかん}（　）{勉強|べんきょう}しています。
notes: へ marks direction of movement.
図書館を勉強 = 'study the library'.
に is for existence or arrival, not for where an action happens.
questions.translation: I study at the library every day.

questions.prompt: {本|ほん}は{机|つくえ}の{上|うえ}（　）あります。
notes: を marks objects of actions.
へ marks direction.
で is for actions/events — a book lying there isn't an event.
questions.translation: The book is on the desk.

questions.prompt: {入口|いりぐち}（　）{靴|くつ}を{脱|ぬ}いでください。
questions.explanation: Taking off shoes is an action → **で**.
notes: 入口に脱ぐ isn't natural — に would mark where the shoes end up, not where you do it.
入口を脱ぐ = 'take off the entrance'.
へ marks direction.
questions.translation: Please take off your shoes at the entrance.

questions.prompt: {日本|にほん}で{一番|いちばん}{大|おお}きい{町|まち}（　）{住|す}んでいます。
questions.explanation: 住む always takes **に**, even though 'live' sounds like an action.
notes: へ marks direction.
町で住んでいます is a very common mistake — 住む is treated like いる.
を doesn't go with 住む.
questions.translation: I live in the biggest city in Japan.

questions.prompt: わたしの{家族|かぞく}は{父|ちち}（　）{母|はは}とわたしの{三人|さんにん}です。
notes: か means 'or'.
や implies 'and others' — contradicts exactly three people.
父も母と isn't a list structure.
questions.translation: My family is three people: my father, my mother and me.

questions.prompt: {友達|ともだち}（　）{一緒|いっしょ}に{映画|えいが}を{見|み}ました。
notes: 友達の一緒 isn't grammatical.
か means 'or'.
や only lists nouns — it can't mean 'together with'.
questions.translation: I watched a movie together with a friend.

questions.prompt: かばんに{本|ほん}（　）ノート（　）が{入|はい}っています。(…among other things)
notes: と…や isn't a list pattern.
や…と isn't a list pattern.
と makes a complete list — clashes with 'among other things'.
questions.translation: There are books, notebooks and so on in my bag.

questions.prompt: わたしは{日本語|にほんご}（　）{少|すこ}しわかります。
questions.explanation: わかる is a state verb → **が**.
notes: に doesn't mark what is understood.
日本語でわかります = 'understand (it) in Japanese'.
日本語をわかります is a classic mistake.

questions.prompt: {新|あたら}しいパソコン（　）ほしいです。
questions.explanation: ほしい is an adjective → **が**.
notes: で would mean 'by means of a computer'.
に doesn't mark the thing wanted.
をほしい is wrong — use を with 買いたい instead.

questions.prompt: {母|はは}は{料理|りょうり}（　）{上手|じょうず}です。
questions.explanation: 上手 is a な-adjective → **が**.
notes: に doesn't mark the skill.
上手 isn't a verb — 料理を上手 is wrong.
で would mean 'by means of cooking'.
questions.translation: My mother is good at cooking.

questions.prompt: {毎朝|まいあさ}{新聞|しんぶん}（　）{読|よ}みます。
questions.explanation: 読む is an action verb → **を**.
notes: が would make the newspaper the reader.
に doesn't mark the thing read.
で would mean 'by means of the newspaper'.
questions.translation: I read the newspaper every morning.
